title: Bournemouth sign Lewis Cook from Leeds for fee rising to £10m
trail: Bournemouth have signed the England Under-19s midfielder Lewis Cook from Leeds for an initial £6m fee, on a four-year contract
body: Bournemouth have signed the Leeds United midfielder Lewis Cook on a four-year contract, for an initial £6m fee. The deal is expected to rise to nearer £10m with add-ons. Leeds rejected a bid from Bournemouth for the England Under-19s star in January. The 19-year-old had been a long-term target for Eddie Howe, who had personally scouted the Leeds youngster on several occasions last season. Cook flew from Leeds’ Dublin training camp on Friday to complete a medical and to finalise a deal, that is understood see him more than treble his wages. Cook, who had been at Leeds since the age of seven, had been persuaded by Garry Monk to spend pre-season with the Yorkshire club instead of preparing for England’s Under-19 European Championship finals, which begin on Sunday, with Aidy Boothroyd’s 18-man squad. Cook joins the France Under-20 striker Lys Mousset, Nathan Aké and Emerson Hyndman in joining the Cherries, following the departures of captain Tommy Elphick and the winger Matt Ritchie. “We’re pleased to be bringing one of the country’s brightest prospects to the club,” said the Bournemouth chief executive Neill Blake. “Lewis has impressed since earning his spot in the Leeds United first-team and we feel that he can continue his rapid progress under the tutelage of Eddie [Howe] and Jason [Tindall].” Bournemouth could yet make the Liverpool winger Jordon Ibe their new record signing, after a £15m fee was agreed between the two clubs on Thursday. Bournemouth are also understood to maintain an interest in the Reading defender Jordan Obita and Tottenham’s Ryan Mason. Leeds signed the forward Kemar Roofe from Oxford and Matt Grimes on loan from Swansea on Thursday, paving the way for Cook’s departure, that was sanctioned by the club’s chairman, Massimo Cellino. Meanwhile, the Leeds left-back Charlie Taylor is a target for Middlesbrough and West Bromwich Albion. Cook will join his Bournemouth team-mates in flying to America on Sunday for their 14-day pre-season tour of Chicago and Minnesota. Cook scored two goals in 85 appearances for his boyhood club.
